properties.decision: Take a claim when you need one and start — but publish it by pushing it, every time, not only when contested; a claim nobody can see is not a claim. When two claims cross, the winner is whichever landed first in git history, and both parties can verify that independently. Rejected: a coordination service or lock manager (contradicts dec:multi-writer-architecture, and single-writer exclusion is the observed failure), and asking before every claim (the fleet measured that timidity starves the pool).
properties.name: Seats coordinate by announcement and provable order, never by exclusion
properties.rationale: The StoryFlow fleet runs 15+ concurrent seats on exactly this rule — grab-and-go, announce always, crossings settled "first-on-disk, both provable". reflow2 has better material for the provable half than a markdown timestamp: a content-hash chain and git order. The alternative people reach for by reflex is a lock, and a lock is exactly what took five of six sessions offline on 2026-07-25.
